name: Spirulina
short: Reviews disagree: one found no acute or chronic toxicity, another warns of adverse effects from toxins (microcystins, BMAA). Single case reports describe anaphylaxis and rhabdomyolysis.
text: Reviews of spirulina reach different conclusions: one nutritional and toxicological review stated that it has not exhibited acute or chronic toxicities and is safe for human consumption, while a later review cautioned that it may have adverse effects due to toxins (microcystins and BMAA), which might contribute to acute poisoning, cancer, liver damage and gastrointestinal disturbances. The same review states that long-term consumption of spirulina may also lead to the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease; its abstract gives no study, study type or figures in support of this statement, so it is reported here as that review's caution and not as an established effect. Reports of serious reactions are single case reports: a 17-year-old male who developed anaphylaxis the first time he took a spirulina tablet, with skin prick testing confirming allergy to the alga rather than the tablet additives, and a first reported case of acute rhabdomyolysis (muscle breakdown) after taking spirulina as a dietary supplement. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
